text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Greek Cypriot newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Preparations expected to start for proximity talks on Cyprus problem in 1997.
- Six people arrested in Limassol; terrorist actions were expected.
- Football stations to start covering Cyprus match league.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Health minister moots introducing charges for prescriptions.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash tells Greek side to give up any thought of Hellenising Cyprus.
- August killings in Dherinia village accentuate inhabitants' concern for safety, says mayor.
HARAVGHI
- Europe pushes for dialogue on Cyprus.
- Petroleum companies switch to blackmail tactics, threatening to leave market without petrol unless government suspends special levy.
- Austrian tour organisation goes bust, leaving huge debts to Cypriot hoteliers.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Washington moving on sidelines to prepare ground for confidential consultations on Cyprus issue.
- Trade unions dismiss proposals to grant cost of living allowance payments only once a year instead of twice.
SIMERINI
- Possibility of informal talks or confidential consultations likely on Cyprus issue.
- Millionaires get documents from community leaders making them eligible for free state healthcare.
- Clash looks likely on petrol prices dispute.
